title: Saturation snapshot collector v1: metrics-backend integration + dashboard links + delayed-metrics fallback
author: Jacob Stein
description:
Context
This PR adds the Saturation Snapshot Collector (v1) to the incident bot. The collector queries the metrics backend for a small set of standardized saturation signals (GPU pressure, queue depth, throttling, scheduler contention, and KV cache pressure where available), formats a compact snapshot suitable for the first 2–5 minutes of triage, and includes deep links to the canonical saturation dashboards.

Motivation
A recurring failure mode in high-sev incidents is spending the first minutes answering: “are we saturated?” (and in which region?) before we can choose a safe mitigation (degrade, shed load, route away, pause rollout, etc.). This is especially painful when 429s / queueing / latency spikes are driven by GPU queue depth and scheduler contention (see SUP-4933). We want the bot to surface a time-bounded snapshot of the most relevant saturation evidence without responders needing to pivot into dashboards immediately.

What’s included
- SaturationCollector (plugin) using the collector framework from #123.
- Metrics backend integration:
  - Adds a thin MetricsQueryClient with bounded retries/backoff and a hard request timeout enforced by the collector framework.
  - Queries a limited set of pre-approved queries (no free-form query strings) to avoid accidental high-cardinality explosions and to make reviewable changes.
- Snapshot semantics:
  - Default window: last 5 minutes, sampled as “most recent datapoint” for each metric (plus timestamp and data age).
  - Reports per impacted (service, region). No per-model or per-route breakdown in v1 (keeps the snapshot readable and avoids cardinality/ambiguity during early triage).
  - Highlights “delayed metrics” explicitly when the newest sample is older than the staleness threshold (default 180s). When delayed, the section still posts with clear caveats and links to dashboards.
- Dashboard links:
  - “Saturation overview” deep link with (service, region, window) pre-selected.
  - “Queue depth / throttling” deep link for fast follow-up during 429/latency incidents.
  - Links are always included even when metrics are delayed/unavailable.
- Fail-open behavior:
  - If the metrics backend returns partial results, we render what we have and include per-signal missing-data lines (e.g., “scheduler_contended: unavailable (no series)”).
  - If the backend is unavailable or times out, we render a minimal section: “Saturation snapshot unavailable (metrics backend timeout)” plus dashboard links and a request id.

Example Slack output (sanitized)
Saturation snapshot (last 5m) • as of 13:22:10Z (age: 48s)
- gateway-api / us-east-1
  - GPU util: 92% (p95)
  - GPU queue depth: 148 (p95)
  - Throttling: 6.3% requests throttled
  - Scheduler contention: elevated
  - KV cache pressure: 0.78
  - Dashboards: overview • queue/throttle
- gateway-api / eu-west-1
  - Metrics delayed (newest sample age: 6m 12s). Treat values as stale.
  - Dashboards: overview • queue/throttle

Notes / guardrails
- No customer payloads or request content are queried or logged. The collector only reads aggregate infra/service metrics.
- No alerting thresholds are introduced here; this is “context only”. Any “elevated” classification is conservative and designed to prompt dashboard follow-up, not to declare root cause.
- Cardinality guardrails: queries are fixed and label sets are constrained to (service, region) only for v1.

Configuration
- configs/collector_defaults.yaml
  - saturation_collector.enabled: true (behind global bot enable flag)
  - saturation_collector.window_minutes: 5
  - saturation_collector.stale_after_seconds: 180
  - saturation_collector.max_regions: 3 (keeps bundles readable)

Testing
- Unit tests for:
  - staleness detection + delayed-metrics rendering
  - partial backend responses and missing-series behavior
  - stable Slack formatting (snapshot tests)
- Fixture-based tests for representative metrics responses (ok/partial/delayed/timeout).

Rollout
- Safe to enable for beta rotations after the saturation dashboards are live in all primary regions.
- Follow-ups:
  - Add better per-signal definitions aligned to the saturation standard doc once finalized (KV cache and scheduler contention naming in particular).
  - Add opt-in per-route/per-model breakdown for “deep diagnostics” command (not part of the default bundle).
commits: collectors: add SaturationCollector v1 and wire into context bundle section ordering
integrations: implement MetricsQueryClient with bounded timeout/retry and fixed query allowlist
formatting: add saturation snapshot Slack renderer + delayed-metrics messaging
dashboards: add link builder for saturation overview and queue/throttle dashboards
configs: add saturation_collector defaults (window + staleness threshold + caps)
tests: add fixtures for metrics responses and unit tests for staleness/partial rendering
docs: add saturation collector troubleshooting notes and examples
review_conversation: Logan Wright (review): Two requests: (1) please make delayed metrics extremely explicit (we’ve been burned by stale samples), and (2) do not introduce per-model labels in the bot output. We can add drill-down later, but the snapshot needs to remain stable and low-cardinality.

Jacob Stein (author): Done. Added staleness detection (default 180s) and a dedicated “Metrics delayed” line that renders even when values exist. Also constrained queries + rendering to (service, region) only for v1; no model/route labels.

Allison Grant (review): Can you confirm the queries align with the saturation standard naming (GPU util vs occupancy, queue depth, throttling)? Also, avoid implying causality—wording should be “elevated”/“high” but not “root cause suspected”.

Jacob Stein (author): Updated wording to be non-assertive (“elevated” with a hint to check dashboards). For GPU we’re using utilization (p95) as the default signal; I added a TODO and an inline comment to revisit occupancy once the backend provides a consistent series across hardware types.
Rafael Mendes (review): What happens when metrics backend lags during a large incident? I don’t want the bot to time out and drop the entire bundle section silently.

Jacob Stein (author): Collector fails open and renders a minimal section with explicit error (timeout/unavailable) + request id + dashboard links. If only some signals time out/miss series, we render the rest and mark missing ones line-by-line.

Caleb Johnson (review): Please ensure we’re not doing N queries per region per signal in a way that scales poorly. Can we batch into a small number of backend requests? Also ensure request timeout is < per-collector timeout so we don’t waste wall clock.

Jacob Stein (author): Client batches signals per (service, region) into a single backend request where supported; otherwise it uses a small fixed set of calls (still bounded). Also set backend timeout to 700ms inside a 1200ms collector budget to leave time for formatting and retries.
Sean Gallagher (review): Slack formatting looks good. Please cap the number of regions printed; some incidents span many regions and threads get unreadable.
Jacob Stein (author): Added saturation_collector.max_regions default=3 (sorted by impacted regions from incident context). Additional regions are summarized as “+N more (see dashboard)”.
Logan Wright (review): Approved after delayed-metrics messaging and query allowlist.
release_notes: Internal-only: incident bot can now attach a saturation snapshot section (GPU pressure/queue depth/throttling/contended scheduler) with dashboard links and explicit handling for delayed metrics.
